blocks.text: Here are reference screenshots of a real-time infrastructure grid: one row per server, with a Server ID, a Name, a Performance Metrics group (a CPU History sparkline, CPU %, Memory %, Disk %, and Response time) and a Status badge. The whole grid updates in real time, roughly every 300ms, and I want the sparkline drawn with d3 as a single <svg> <path>. On the right there's a column panel that controls the layout - show/hide, pin, and reorder columns. The reference design is rough, so you have full freedom to build a clean, Linear-style grid.

I studied the seven references and the renderer APIs. It's a flat table - one row per host, scrolling - with a two-level column header where a Performance Metrics band spans five child columns. Here's the aspect inventory I reconstructed before I ask a few scoping questions:

rows: Shape
Flat table, one row per server; a 2-level header with a Performance Metrics band over 5 child columns
Columns
Server ID · Name · Performance Metrics → [CPU History · CPU % · Memory % · Disk % · Response (ms)] · Status
Pinning
Server ID pinned left, Status pinned right; data scrolls under both, and pin state is reconfigurable from the panel
Realtime
Updates every 300ms - numeric metrics tick and CPU History is a d3 line sparkline (single <path>) that shifts new points in
Encodings
Heat pills on CPU / Memory, plain Disk, latency-colored Response text, a Status badge, and a blue CPU sparkline
Column panel
A collapsed vertical Columns tab: search box, PINNED LEFT / MAIN / PINNED RIGHT sections, per-row visibility + drag handle + L/R pins, Reset
Header filters
A funnel per column - text (Contains), number (Equals), status (multi-select)

blocks.text: A few scoping decisions before I write the implementation brief - my best guess is pre-selected in each:

items.question: Which column-panel controls should be fully functional?
items.answer: Show/hide columns, pin left / right, drag to reorder, and the search box

items.question: Should the column-header filter funnels be functional (text / number / status)?
Should clicking a column header sort the grid?
items.answer: Sorting for number / measure fields only

items.question: What visual design direction for the grid and chrome?

blocks.text: Going with those. Here's how each aspect maps to a grid mechanism - viewmodel-only, no DataSource or DataModel:

rows: Shape
Grid(flat) + FlattenedDataViewModel; 2-level columnFacets - grouped columns share a Performance Metrics band, solo columns span both header rows
Realtime 300ms
setInterval mutates the server objects in place and shifts each sparkline's ring buffer, then grid.draw() (row order stays fixed)
CPU sparkline
A cell renderer builds one <svg><path>; d comes from d3-shape line() + d3-scale scaleLinear
CPU / Memory
Heat-scaled pill; Disk is plain numeric; Response is latency-colored text; Status is a pill badge
Left/right pinning
Pinned columns render through pooled PVerticalFixtures; the Grid is reconstructed only when a side's fixture count changes, else vm-rebuild + draw
Column panel + filters
A right rail collapsible Columns tab; each header funnel opens a text / number / status popup
Sorting
Numeric headers only, via delegated pointerdown (onclick is wiped by the 300ms redraw)
Theme
A custom Linear-style light/dark pair that follows the page theme

blocks.text: All header interaction is event-delegated on the stable grid mount so the redraw can't swallow it. Building it now with self-contained generated data and light/dark counterparts.

The horizontal scroll stops working once I pin columns - fix the column sizing so the grid still scrolls under the pinned columns. Also change how the sparkline builds up: instead of starting full of random values, start empty and accumulate one point per tick, keeping past points fixed and only sliding the window once it fills - like t1:[], t2:[5], t3:[5,10], t4:[5,10,6], t5:[10,6,3].

Two changes. First, sizing: I moved the main columns to content width (max-cell) so the main region stays wide enough to scroll under the pinned fixtures, and capped the two elastic columns (Name and CPU History) with a max width. Second, the sparkline now starts empty and accumulates - each tick pushes the live CPU value and only drops the oldest once the window fills, so past points stay fixed exactly like your t1:[] → … → t5:[10,6,3]. I also guard the sub-2-point case so an empty history renders nothing instead of a stray mark.

A few visual fixes: right-align all the numbers; left-align the status pills; the Server ID and Name cells need left padding; the line chart looks broken and cut in the middle - turn it into a smooth area chart by closing the curve and using a Catmull-Rom style interpolation in d3; make the column panel thinner so the grid gets more space when it's open; and when Name is hidden the Performance Metrics group header goes misaligned.

All six done. Numbers are right-aligned, status is left-aligned, and Server ID / Name now carry left padding. The sparkline is now a smooth Catmull-Rom area + line - two paths in a fixed coordinate space, stretched to the cell width with preserveAspectRatio="none":

I narrowed the column panel so the grid gets more room, and fixed the misaligned group band: any change to the column set (hiding Name included) now rebuilds the grid from scratch, so no stale rowspan header cell survives to shift the Performance Metrics band. Row-only changes (sort/filter) still update in place.
When I unpin a column and it ends up as the last column, that column isn't fully visible - I can't scroll far enough to see all of it.

This was a real width-accounting bug. The grid derives its scrollable width from each column's measured leaf header cell - data cells are never measured, and non-leaf (rowspan) header cells aren't either. Non-grouped columns were structured as level0 = key, level1 = null, i.e. a single tall header cell spanning both rows - a non-leaf cell. So the grid never measured those columns and fell back to defaultCellWidth (50px) in its total-width math while CSS rendered them at real content width. The total came out short, so the scroll range couldn't reach the end - worst when such a column landed last.

The fix: give every column a measured leaf header (non-grouped → level0 = "", level1 = key; grouped stay under the Performance Metrics band) and use deterministic fixed widths, so measured-leaf == CSS track == data-cell width. The scroll math is now exact and the last column is fully reachable after any unpin. This also retro-fixes the earlier "scroll not working when pinning" report - it was the same measurement bug.
The pinned columns are fine now. But if I drag Name to the end (just before the pinned column) and move CPU History to the end too, the header layout breaks.

With Name dragged into the middle and CPU History moved to the end, the Performance Metrics group's members were no longer contiguous - indices 0,1,2,3 then 5, with Name's blank cell at 4. That produced two separate Performance Metrics bands, and the grid's sticky band-label centering shifted both labels to stay in view, so they overlapped and the header looked broken. The fix: only render the group band when its visible members form a single contiguous run; otherwise those columns fall back to ungrouped (blank top strip).

So when the metrics stay together the band shows; split them and each column shows its own header with a blank strip above - no split bands, no overlapping labels. Reordering them back (or Reset columns) brings the band back.

Let's turn this into a proper terminal-style grid:
1. Update once per second instead of every 300ms.
2. The sparkline still has a jagged, sawtooth movement - figure out whether that's the data generation or the line rendering, fix it, and apply a Catmull-Rom style interpolation.
3. Make the whole grid compact and monospace - a terminal look.
4. Drop the pills around the numbers; instead show a small colored circle plus the value in that same color. Off-white terminal look for light, Monokai for dark, with bright green / red highlights.
5. Drop the status pills too - same idea: a rounded-rect solid swatch followed by colored text.
6. Make the numbers bold.
7. Chart color should be bright green.
8. Tighten the row padding for compactness, fade the column borders a lot, and use slightly less-faded blue row borders.

Full terminal-vibe redesign. The sawtooth was a data-gen issue - a raw random walk zig-zags point to point - so I gave the CPU a momentum-driven walk: velocity carries over between ticks, with mean reversion toward 50 and a soft bounce at the edges, so the curve trends in smooth arcs before the Catmull-Rom spline even smooths it:

The rest: tick is now 1s; the grid is compact and monospace throughout; the number pills are gone in favor of a colored dot + the value in that same color, bold; the status pills became a rounded-rect swatch + colored label; the sparkline is bright green. Column (vertical) borders are faded almost to nothing and the row (horizontal) borders read as subtle blue rules. Light mode is an off-white terminal, dark mode is Monokai-style.

A few more:
- Extend the faint vertical column line into the pinned fixture columns by drawing the border on the fixture cell itself.
- The chart looks like it's drawing the old array and the new array on top of each other - if the data generation already keeps the array correct, just repaint the chart cleanly.
- Make the blue horizontal row borders a bit more prominent.
- Move the heat dot to the left of the number cells (with padding), keeping the number on the right.
- The theme doesn't feel right - switch to Gruvbox dark / light colors, keeping the bright font / heat colors you're already using.

You were exactly right about the chart - the sparkline renderer returns void (it owns the cell), but it was calling appendChild, so every redraw stacked a new SVG on top of the old ones. Switched to replaceChildren, so each tick just repaints the current window; the ring buffer was already correct:

The vertical line now continues into the fixtures (a border on the side of each pinned cell facing the data), the blue row borders are more prominent, and the number cells use space-between so the heat dot pins left (with padding) and the bold value pins right. And I replaced the theme with a Gruvbox pair - dark #282828 / #ebdbb2, light around #f9f8f4 / #3a3733 - keeping the bright Gruvbox heat and status colors.

Dark theme is great, but the light theme is too solarized and yellow - I want a subtle off-white, creamish look. Also:
1. The chart fills from left to right (probably array length) - it should stream from right to left with a fixed-length array padded with zeros, filling from the end.
2. The vertical lines still don't extend into the fixtures - I think there's a grid CSS rule forcing border-top: none on the fixture cells.
3. For the metric numbers, render the healthy (currently green) ones in the normal text color so there aren't too many colors, and only color the warning and critical numbers; keep the status colors as they are.

Light theme is now a calm off-white cream (surface #f9f8f4, warm-dark text #3a3733) instead of the yellow solarized look; dark stays Gruvbox. The chart streams right→left: cpuHistory is a fixed-length, zero-padded ring buffer, each tick pushes the newest value onto the end and shifts the oldest off the front, so new data enters at the right edge and ages leftward.

You found the fixture border cause - grid.css sets border-top: none on .left-fixture / .right-fixture cells, which killed the horizontal rule in the pinned columns. The fixture data cells now re-apply it inline (skipping the top row, matching the .first data cells), so both the blue row rules and the faint column rules are continuous across Server ID / Status:

And the numbers are calmer: healthy values now render in the normal text color, only warning (amber) and critical (red) values take their color, while the little severity dot still always carries the heat color. Status colors are unchanged.
